# `ossready` commands

Every command takes an optional `[directory]` (default: the current directory). `ossready --help` and `ossready <command> --help` print the same options in a terminal, and `ossready --version` prints the installed version. The checks that `ossready doctor` runs are in [checks.md](checks.md).

- [`ossready init`](#ossready-init): Scaffold a production-ready GitHub repo
- [`ossready doctor`](#ossready-doctor): Audit an existing repo for missing OSS-readiness files
- [`ossready sync`](#ossready-sync): Update ossready-managed workflows, Dependabot and Issue Forms to the current templates (dry run unless `--write`)
- [`ossready badges`](#ossready-badges): Print README badges (CI, npm, license, Scorecard, CodeQL) for a repo

## `ossready init`

Scaffold a production-ready GitHub repo.

Usage: `ossready init [directory] [options]`

Options:

- `--name <name>`: Project / package name
- `--description <text>`: Short project description
- `--author <name>`: Copyright holder for LICENSE and CITATION.cff authors
- `--license <license>`: License: mit | apache-2.0 (default: mit)
- `--package-manager <pm>`: Package manager: npm | pnpm | yarn | bun (default: npm)
- `--coc-email <email>`: Code of Conduct contact email (default: conduct@example.com)
- `--security-email <email>`: Private security contact email for SECURITY.md
- `--github-owner <owner>`: GitHub username or org for README badges, URLs, CODEOWNERS, FUNDING.yml, CITATION.cff, SUPPORT.md, and SECURITY.md
- `-y, --yes`: Skip interactive prompts and use defaults for omitted options
- `--force`: Overwrite existing files
- `--dry-run`: Print planned files without writing

Examples:

```bash
ossready init my-lib
ossready init my-lib --yes --license apache-2.0 --package-manager pnpm
ossready init . --dry-run
```

## `ossready doctor`

Audit an existing repo for missing OSS-readiness files.

Every check is described in [checks.md](checks.md), and `ossready doctor --list` prints the same catalogue.

Usage: `ossready doctor [directory] [options]`

Options:

- `--json`: Print the report as JSON
- `--markdown`: Print the report as Markdown (for GitHub job summaries and PR comments)
- `--strict`: Also fail (exit 1) when recommended checks are missing
- `--fix`: Write missing files from ossready's templates (never overwrites)
- `--dry-run`: With `--fix`: list files that would be written
- `--github-owner <owner>`: GitHub owner for `--fix` and the readme-badges check (default: from package.json or git remote)
- `--author <name>`: With `--fix`: copyright holder (default: package.json author)
- `--license <license>`: With `--fix`: mit | apache-2.0 (default: package.json license)
- `--coc-email <email>`: With `--fix`: Code of Conduct contact email
- `--security-email <email>`: With `--fix`: private security contact email for SECURITY.md
- `--list`: List every check (id, level, description, `--fix` support) without auditing; add `--json` for JSON

Examples:

```bash
ossready doctor .
ossready doctor . --strict --json
ossready doctor . --markdown >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
ossready doctor . --fix --dry-run
ossready doctor --list
```

## `ossready sync`

Update ossready-managed workflows, Dependabot and Issue Forms to the current templates (dry run unless `--write`).

Usage: `ossready sync [directory] [options]`

Options:

- `--write`: Apply the changes (default: dry run with a diff per file; exits 1 when changes are pending)
- `--add-missing`: Also create managed files that don't exist yet
- `--force`: Also overwrite files without the ossready marker line
- `--quiet`: One summary line per file instead of diffs
- `--json`: Print the result as JSON
- `--github-owner <owner>`: GitHub owner for owner-bound files (default: package.json links or the origin remote)
- `--package-manager <pm>`: npm | pnpm | yarn | bun (default: from lockfiles or package.json packageManager)

Examples:

```bash
ossready sync .
ossready sync . --quiet
ossready sync . --write
```

## `ossready badges`

Print README badges (CI, npm, license, Scorecard, CodeQL) for a repo.

Usage: `ossready badges [directory] [options]`

Options:

- `--write`: Insert or update the badge block in README.md between ossready markers
- `--dry-run`: With `--write`: show what would change without writing
- `--json`: Print the badges as JSON
- `--github-owner <owner>`: GitHub owner (default: package.json links, git remotes, or git config github.user)
- `--repo <repo>`: Repository name or `<owner>/<name>` (default: from package.json links or the origin remote)

Examples:

```bash
ossready badges .
ossready badges . --write --dry-run
ossready badges . --write --github-owner octo
```
